display_name: Revolving consumer credit (SA)
scope_note: Fed G.19 revolving consumer credit, all holders (banks, credit unions, finance companies, nonfinancial businesses). Mostly credit cards but not only. Seasonally adjusted, billions.

display_name: Revolving consumer credit (NSA)
scope_note: Fed G.19 revolving consumer credit, all holders, not seasonally adjusted, billions.

display_name: Total consumer credit (SA)
scope_note: Fed G.19 total consumer credit (revolving plus nonrevolving), all holders, seasonally adjusted, billions.

display_name: Card APR, all accounts
scope_note: Fed G.19 commercial bank interest rate on credit card plans, all accounts. Quarterly survey taken in the middle month of the quarter; here dated to the quarter end.

display_name: Card APR, accounts assessed interest
scope_note: Fed G.19 commercial bank interest rate on credit card plans, accounts assessed interest (revolvers only). Quarterly survey, middle month of the quarter, dated to quarter end.

display_name: Card charge-off rate, all commercial banks (SA)
scope_note: Fed charge-off and delinquency release. Net charge-offs on credit card loans, annualized, as % of average loans, all insured US commercial banks. Seasonally adjusted.

display_name: Card charge-off rate, top 100 banks (SA)
scope_note: Fed charge-off and delinquency release. Net charge-offs on credit card loans, annualized, 100 largest commercial banks by assets. Seasonally adjusted.

display_name: Card charge-off rate, banks outside top 100 (SA)
scope_note: Fed charge-off and delinquency release. Net charge-offs on credit card loans, annualized, commercial banks outside the 100 largest. Small base and volatile. Seasonally adjusted.

display_name: Card delinquency rate, all commercial banks (SA)
scope_note: Fed charge-off and delinquency release. Credit card loans 30+ days past due as % of card loans, end of quarter, all insured US commercial banks. Seasonally adjusted.

display_name: Card delinquency rate, top 100 banks (SA)
scope_note: Fed charge-off and delinquency release. Credit card loans 30+ days past due, 100 largest commercial banks. Seasonally adjusted.

display_name: Card delinquency rate, banks outside top 100 (SA)
scope_note: Fed charge-off and delinquency release. Credit card loans 30+ days past due, commercial banks outside the 100 largest. Seasonally adjusted.

display_name: SLOOS: net % of banks tightening card standards
scope_note: Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey, domestic banks. Net percentage tightening standards for credit card loans: positive means more banks tightened than eased. Each survey asks about the previous three months, so the July survey (which FRED dates to Q3) is shown at June 30: period offset -1 in series.csv, applied by the FRED fetcher.

display_name: Credit card loans at commercial banks, weekly (SA)
scope_note: Fed H.8 assets and liabilities of commercial banks: credit card and other revolving plans, all commercial banks, seasonally adjusted, billions. Weeks ending Wednesday. Banks only, so narrower than G.19. The level jump in March 2010 is securitized card balances being consolidated onto bank balance sheets (FAS 166/167), not new lending.

display_name: Credit card loans at commercial banks, monthly (SA)
scope_note: Fed H.8: credit card and other revolving plans, all commercial banks, seasonally adjusted, monthly average, billions. The level jump in March 2010 is securitized card balances being consolidated onto bank balance sheets (FAS 166/167), not new lending.

display_name: Household debt service ratio
scope_note: Federal Reserve Board household debt service ratio: required payments on outstanding mortgage and consumer debt as a percentage of disposable personal income, seasonally adjusted. The Board's own estimate, published about five months after the quarter. This is the burden measure: a card balance is only a problem relative to the income servicing it.

display_name: Consumer debt service ratio
scope_note: Federal Reserve Board consumer debt service ratio: required payments on non-mortgage consumer debt (cards, auto, student) as a percentage of disposable personal income, seasonally adjusted. The card share of this is not published separately.

display_name: Disposable personal income (SA, annual rate)
scope_note: Bureau of Economic Analysis disposable personal income, seasonally adjusted annual rate, billions. Used as the denominator for card debt relative to income; because it is an annual rate, the ratio reads as card balances per dollar of annual after-tax income.

display_name: Personal saving rate
scope_note: Bureau of Economic Analysis personal saving as a percentage of disposable personal income, seasonally adjusted. Context for whether households have a buffer behind the card balance.

display_name: Consumer price index (all urban, SA)
scope_note: Bureau of Labor Statistics CPI for all urban consumers, seasonally adjusted, 1982-84 = 100. Used only to restate card balances in today's dollars; nothing on the page is deflated silently.

display_name: Unemployment rate
scope_note: Bureau of Labor Statistics civilian unemployment rate, seasonally adjusted. The single best external predictor of card losses: charge-offs are a job-loss phenomenon more than an interest-rate one.

display_name: Consumer sentiment (Michigan)
scope_note: University of Michigan index of consumer sentiment, 1966 Q1 = 100. Not seasonally adjusted. Included because stated sentiment and card behaviour have diverged sharply since 2022 and the gap is itself a finding.

display_name: Bank prime loan rate
scope_note: The rate posted by a majority of the largest banks, monthly. Most variable-rate card APRs are set as prime plus a margin, so card APR minus prime is the margin the issuer actually sets and the part that is not explained by monetary policy.

display_name: Advertised card APR (Bankrate, weekly)
scope_note: Bankrate's weekly survey of advertised purchase APRs on a fixed panel of about 100 widely available cards, via FRED. Advertised terms on new offers, not rates paid on balances, and a different population from both the Fed's G.19 survey and the CFPB's card-terms survey. Weekly, so it is the earliest read on pricing.

display_name: Consumer loan charge-off rate (SA)
scope_note: Federal Reserve Board net charge-off rate on all consumer loans at commercial banks, annualized, seasonally adjusted. Cards are the largest and worst-performing part of this, so the gap between the card rate and this one says whether card stress is idiosyncratic or part of a broader consumer credit cycle.

display_name: Consumer loan delinquency rate (SA)
scope_note: Federal Reserve Board delinquency rate on all consumer loans at commercial banks, 30 or more days past due, seasonally adjusted. The broader consumer comparator for the card delinquency rate.

display_name: Nonrevolving consumer credit (SA)
scope_note: Fed G.19 nonrevolving consumer credit (auto and student loans, mostly), all holders, seasonally adjusted, billions. The other half of consumer credit: revolving growing faster than nonrevolving is a different economy from the reverse.

Placeholder APRs (0, 9.99) are dropped.

display_name: Applied for a credit card (all respondents)
scope_note: Share who applied for a credit card in the past twelve months. New York Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations, Credit Access Survey, fielded every four months in February, June and October to the SCE panel of about 1,100 household heads, weighted to be nationally representative. Each reading covers the twelve months up to and including the survey month and is dated to the last day of that month. Asked of all respondents.

display_name: Requested a credit limit increase (all respondents)
scope_note: Share who asked for an increase in a credit card limit in the past twelve months. New York Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations, Credit Access Survey, fielded every four months in February, June and October to the SCE panel of about 1,100 household heads, weighted to be nationally representative. Each reading covers the twelve months up to and including the survey month and is dated to the last day of that month. Asked of all respondents.

display_name: Applied for any credit (all respondents)
scope_note: Share who applied for at least one type of credit (card, mortgage, refinance, auto or other) in the past twelve months. New York Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations, Credit Access Survey, fielded every four months in February, June and October to the SCE panel of about 1,100 household heads, weighted to be nationally representative. Each reading covers the twelve months up to and including the survey month and is dated to the last day of that month. Asked of all respondents.

display_name: Rejected for any credit, of those who applied (all respondents)
scope_note: Share of applicants who were turned down by at least one lender in the past twelve months. The denominator is applicants, not all respondents, so it is a rejection rate and not a share of the population. New York Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations, Credit Access Survey, fielded every four months in February, June and October to the SCE panel of about 1,100 household heads, weighted to be nationally representative. Each reading covers the twelve months up to and including the survey month and is dated to the last day of that month. Asked of all respondents.

display_name: Discouraged from applying (all respondents)
scope_note: Share who needed credit but did not apply because they expected to be rejected. Discouragement is invisible in lender data: a household that never applies never appears in an approval rate. New York Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations, Credit Access Survey, fielded every four months in February, June and October to the SCE panel of about 1,100 household heads, weighted to be nationally representative. Each reading covers the twelve months up to and including the survey month and is dated to the last day of that month. Asked of all respondents.

display_name: Had an account closed by a lender (all respondents)
scope_note: Share who had at least one account closed by the lender in the past twelve months. A supply measure that no lender-reported source publishes. New York Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations, Credit Access Survey, fielded every four months in February, June and October to the SCE panel of about 1,100 household heads, weighted to be nationally representative. Each reading covers the twelve months up to and including the survey month and is dated to the last day of that month. Asked of all respondents.

display_name: Survey respondents (all respondents)
scope_note: Unweighted number of respondents behind the wave's percentages. Published so a reading on a thin cell can be discounted: the sub-680 score bucket runs around 150 respondents against about 500 for the top bucket. New York Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations, Credit Access Survey, fielded every four months in February, June and October to the SCE panel of about 1,100 household heads, weighted to be nationally representative. Each reading covers the twelve months up to and including the survey month and is dated to the last day of that month. Asked of all respondents.

display_name: Rejected for a credit card, of those who applied (all respondents)
scope_note: Share of credit card applicants who were turned down in the past twelve months. Only published for the whole sample, not by credit score. New York Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations, Credit Access Survey, fielded every four months in February, June and October to the SCE panel of about 1,100 household heads, weighted to be nationally representative. Each reading covers the twelve months up to and including the survey month and is dated to the last day of that month. Asked of all respondents.

display_name: Refused a credit limit increase, of those who asked (all respondents)
scope_note: Share of those who asked for a higher credit card limit and were refused. Only published for the whole sample. New York Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations, Credit Access Survey, fielded every four months in February, June and October to the SCE panel of about 1,100 household heads, weighted to be nationally representative. Each reading covers the twelve months up to and including the survey month and is dated to the last day of that month. Asked of all respondents.

display_name: Expected chance of a card application being rejected (all respondents)

Mean of respondents' stated probability (0 to 100) of not being able to make a minimum debt payment over the next three months. A stated probability, not a delinquency rate: its level is far above any measured delinquency, its direction is the signal. Respondents some college; subgroup samples are a few hundred a month, so read three-month averages.
